requirement_snapshot.name: Sign In with an Existing Account
requirement_snapshot.description:
This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-1-1-1 (Register a New GitHub Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. The sign-in page is the form on the account-access page containing “Username or email”, “Password”, and “Sign in”. A “session” is the current-browser login record saved after successful account authentication, represented in the frontend by the upper-right account menu and access to protected pages. The visitor enters a username or email and a password and submits the form. The system looks up the account and validates its credentials and availability status; if authentication fails due to an unknown username/email, incorrect password, or unavailable account, the system displays exactly the same generic failure message “Invalid credentials”, does not disclose whether the account exists or which credential was wrong, and does not create a session. After successful authentication, the system stores a session with a unique session identifier, account identifier, and active status, then redirects to the workspace accessible to that user; the session remains valid after refreshing or reopening the workspace, and subsequent protected organization, repository, and work-item requests must use this session to determine the current user.

Screenshot reference:
![image](reference/github-sign-in.png)

interfaces.name: useSignInForm
interfaces.first_line: export function useSignInForm({ signIn, onSignedIn }: UseSignInFormOptions): UseSignInFormResult {
interfaces.responsibility: Owns sign-in form values, pending state, and the single generic failure message, and delegates state changes to the shared session context.
interfaces.specification: Exports INVALID_CREDENTIALS_MESSAGE = 'Invalid credentials' (exact string used for an unknown username/email, an incorrect password, and an unavailable account), SignInFormValues { identifier, password }, UseSignInFormOptions { signIn, onSignedIn? } and UseSignInFormResult { values, submitting, formError, setField, submit }. submit() sets submitting while in flight and clears it in finally, calls the injected signIn({ identifier, password }) so SessionContext remains the only owner of authenticated state, resolves the SessionUser and calls onSignedIn(user) on success, and on any AuthRequestError sets formError to INVALID_CREDENTIALS_MESSAGE, keeps the typed identifier/password in the inputs, and resolves null without creating local user state. TODO(TDD): implement that catch branch; no other behavior is implemented yet.
inputs: UseSignInFormOptions { signIn: (input: SignInInput) => Promise<SessionUser>, onSignedIn?: (user: SessionUser) => void }
setField(field, value) from the controlled inputs
outputs: UseSignInFormResult { values, submitting, formError, setField, submit }
test_focus: A rejected sign-in renders exactly 'Invalid credentials' and leaves values.identifier/values.password unchanged
Unknown identifier, wrong password and unavailable account all yield the identical message text
formError is null after a successful sign-in and onSignedIn receives the resolved user
submitting returns to false after a rejection so the Sign in button stays actionable

interfaces.name: SignInPage
interfaces.responsibility: Account-access page that renders the username-or-email sign-in form and redirects into the authenticated workspace on success.
interfaces.specification: Routed at '/signin' by frontend/src/App.tsx. Owns exactly one textbox labeled 'Username or email', one password input labeled 'Password' (type=password so it is never echoed) and one enabled button named 'Sign in', all rendered through the reused AuthTextField. On success it navigates (replace) to location.state.from when that is a protected path, otherwise to WORKSPACE_PATH '/workspace'; a rejected attempt stays on the page and shows the single generic message through useSignInForm (role="alert"), and the header account menu must not display a username. Also renders the 'Create an account' link to '/register' that the REQ-1-1-1 registration page already expects. TODO(TDD): wire the redirect and confirm no session state is created on rejection.
inputs: react-router location.state.from for the originally requested protected path
outputs: navigation to the workspace or the requested protected path on success
test_focus: getByLabelText('Username or email'), getByLabelText('Password') and getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }) all resolve
Filling 'alice-dev' with 'Valid-password-123!' lands on /workspace and the header shows alice-dev
Filling 'alice.dev@example.test' with 'Valid-password-123!' also succeeds (email identifier accepted)
A wrong password keeps the page on /signin, shows 'Invalid credentials' and renders no account menu username

interfaces.name: AccountMenu
interfaces.responsibility: Upper-right chrome that is the visible representation of the current-browser session.
interfaces.specification: Consumes the shared session context only (no page-local user state). status 'loading' renders a role="status" placeholder; unauthenticated renders a 'Sign in' link to '/signin'; authenticated renders a button whose accessible name contains the username plus a menu with 'Signed in as {username}' and a 'Sign out' item. TODO(TDD): wire the Sign out item to the shared signOut so the persisted session is cleared and the chrome returns to the unauthenticated state.
test_focus: Fresh unauthenticated browser shows the Sign in link and no username
After a successful sign-in the menu button exposes alice-dev
A failed sign-in never renders an account-menu username

interfaces.name: RequireAuth
interfaces.first_line: export function RequireAuth({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
interfaces.responsibility: Route guard that resolves the current user from the shared session before rendering protected pages.
interfaces.specification: status 'loading' renders a neutral role="status" message instead of redirecting or rendering protected content; 'unauthenticated' renders <Navigate to="/signin" replace state={{ from: location.pathname }} />; 'authenticated' renders children. Because the guard reads the shared context, a successful sign-in restores direct access to a previously visible protected path after refresh, while a failed sign-in still requires authentication.
outputs: protected children or a redirect to /signin carrying the requested path

interfaces.name: authClientSignInAndSession
interfaces.first_line: export async function signIn(input: SignInInput): Promise<SignInResult>
interfaces.responsibility: Frontend HTTP boundary for sign-in and session restore, sending the username-or-email identifier the sign-in form collects.
interfaces.specification: SignInInput is now { identifier: string; password: string } so the exact field name flows from the 'Username or email' input through SessionContext and the POST body to the service lookup (previously the field was named email). signIn() posts /auth/login through the shared axios instance (baseURL '/api'; REQ-1-1-1 contract requires withCredentials so the arc_session cookie round-trips) and resolves { user }. It must throw AuthRequestError carrying status 401 and the server's generic message for any credential rejection, and it must not surface which credential was wrong. fetchCurrentUser() GETs /auth/session, resolves null on 401 and throws on other failures so reload recovery works. signOut() POSTs /auth/logout. TODO(TDD): implement these bodies; they currently throw 'not implemented'.
test_focus: signIn posts { identifier, password } — not the legacy email field — to /api/auth/login
A 401 response produces AuthRequestError whose message is the generic failure text
fetchCurrentUser resolves null on 401 so the provider settles on unauthenticated

interfaces.name: SessionProviderAndUseSession
interfaces.first_line: export function SessionProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
interfaces.responsibility: Global authenticated-state source of truth that the header, route guard, sign-in page and workspace all consume after sign-in.
interfaces.specification: Provides { status: 'loading' | 'authenticated' | 'unauthenticated', user: SessionUser | null, signIn, signOut, refresh }. signIn(input: SignInInput) calls authClient.signIn with the identifier field, publishes the returned user and flips status to 'authenticated' so chrome and protected routes update from this single store. On mount refresh() must call fetchCurrentUser(), tolerate a failed restore by falling back to 'unauthenticated', and never leave status at 'loading'; that reload path is what keeps the signed-in username visible after a refresh or a direct reopen of a protected page. On a rejected sign-in the state must remain 'unauthenticated' with user null. TODO(TDD): implement the mount effect (currently a placeholder `void refresh;`).
outputs: SessionContextValue { status, user, signIn, signOut, refresh }
test_focus: Status settles from loading to unauthenticated when restore returns 401
After signIn resolves, status is authenticated and user.username is alice-dev
A rejected signIn leaves status unauthenticated and user null
useSession outside the provider throws the explicit error message

interfaces.name: AuthTextField

interfaces.name: authRoutesSignInAndSession
interfaces.responsibility: HTTP boundary for sign-in and session restore under /api/auth, returning one non-disclosing failure message.
interfaces.specification: Registered in backend/src/app.js via app.use('/api/auth', require('./routes/auth_routes')). Reused constants: SESSION_COOKIE_NAME = 'arc_session' (httpOnly, sameSite lax, path '/') and REGISTRATION_FIELDS. Additional contract this node owns: SIGN_IN_FIELDS = ['identifier','password'] (field name matches the 'Username or email' input and SignInInput) and INVALID_CREDENTIALS_MESSAGE = 'Invalid credentials'. POST /login accepts { identifier, password } where identifier may be a username or a verified email, resolves the account, validates the password and the account availability status, and on success answers 200 { user: { id, username, email, emailVerified }, session: { token } } and sets the arc_session cookie. Every credential failure — unknown username/email, incorrect password, unavailable account — answers the identical 401 { message: 'Invalid credentials' } (optionally with fieldErrors) and creates no session and no cookie. GET /session resolves the cookie via the service and answers 200 { user } or 401 { message }; POST /logout clears the cookie with 204. No response body or log line may contain the password or reveal which credential failed. TODO(TDD): replace the not-implemented handlers; the exported constants above still need to be added to the module exports.
inputs: JSON body { identifier, password } for POST /login
arc_session cookie for GET /session and POST /logout
test_focus: POST /api/auth/login with alice-dev + Valid-password-123! returns 200, a live cookie and a cookie-usable session
POST /api/auth/login with alice.dev@example.test + Valid-password-123! also returns 200
Unknown identifier, wrong password and unavailable account each return the byte-identical 401 message and set no cookie
GET /api/auth/session with the login cookie returns 200 { user }; without it returns 401

interfaces.name: authServiceCredentialVerificationAndSession
interfaces.responsibility: Authoritative credential verification and session lifecycle: unique session identifier, account identifier and active status.
interfaces.specification: Reuses USERNAME_PATTERN, limits, RegistrationError, validateRegistrationInput, registerUser, hashPassword/verifyPassword and the db_runtime helpers from REQ-1-1-1. Contract this node owns: add INVALID_CREDENTIALS_MESSAGE = 'Invalid credentials' to the exported constants and FIELD_MESSAGES, plus SESSION_ACTIVE = 1 / SESSION_INACTIVE = 0 flags. authenticateUser({ identifier, password }) must resolve the account by username_lower OR email_lower (case-insensitive), verify the password through verifyPassword, reject accounts whose availability status is not available/verified, and return either the public projection { id, username, email, emailVerified } or null — it must return null (never a distinguishable error) for an unknown identifier, a wrong password and an unavailable account so the route can emit one generic message. createSessionForUser(userId) inserts exactly one sessions row with an unguessable unique token (unique session identifier), the account id in user_id, and an active status/expiry derived from SESSION_TTL_MS. getSessionUser(token) returns the linked public user only for a non-expired, active session, otherwise null; destroySession(token) deletes or deactivates the row. No plaintext password may be logged or returned anywhere. TODO(TDD): implement these bodies; they currently throw not-implemented.
callees: node:crypto password verification and token generation
test_focus: authenticateUser accepts both 'alice-dev' and 'alice.dev@example.test' case-insensitively
authenticateUser returns null for an unknown identifier, a wrong password and an unavailable account
createSessionForUser writes one sessions row containing a unique token, the account id and an active status/expiry
getSessionUser returns null for expired/unknown tokens and the correct user for a live one

interfaces.name: AuthSchemaSessionsActiveStatus
interfaces.responsibility: Reused idempotent schema for the account and session records that sign-in must persist.
interfaces.specification: Reused from REQ-1-1-1; no new table is owned by this node. Existing shape: users(id, username, username_lower UNIQUE, email, email_lower UNIQUE, email_verified, password_hash, created_at) and sessions(id, token UNIQUE, user_id REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, created_at, expires_at). This node requires that a session record can carry the unique session identifier (token), the account identifier (user_id) and an active status; if an explicit active flag is needed, add it append-only and guarded (ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN guarded by existence checks) inside initializeDatabase so isolated test DBs created through createTestDatabaseHarness stay identical to production. username_lower/email_lower are what make username-or-email lookup case-insensitive, and password material stays only in password_hash. TODO(TDD): add the guarded active-status column only if the service needs it beyond expires_at.
inputs: optional { dbPath, reset } options from app bootstrap or test harness
outputs: Promise<sqlite3.Database> after users and sessions exist
test_focus: initializeDatabase stays idempotent across repeated startups and on a fresh test DB
username_lower/email_lower uniqueness supports case-insensitive sign-in lookup
Deleting a user cascades its sessions rows

interfaces.name: seedDatabaseSignInAccount
interfaces.responsibility: Reused deterministic bootstrap of the pre-existing sign-in-capable account the scenarios depend on.
interfaces.specification: Reused from REQ-1-1-1 and required unchanged by this node: the GIVEN steps declare that account `alice-dev`, email `alice.dev@example.test`, password `Valid-password-123!`, verified and available, already exists in a fresh browser session. seedDatabase() must therefore create that account through auth_service.ensureVerifiedAccount({ username, email, password }) inside the existing withTransaction callback, idempotently (upsert / INSERT OR IGNORE on username_lower and email_lower) so repeated startups and resets converge on exactly one row and never overwrite a conflicting user-created account. It must run through the normal backend startup path (and the test harness seedDefault), not through a test-only endpoint and not as a frontend constant or fallback array, so POST /api/auth/login and GET /api/auth/session read it through the real service path. Disabled/unavailable-account scenarios must be able to create such a row through this same persistence path rather than a hidden fixture.
inputs: none (reads its own fixed account definition)
outputs: Promise<void> after committing the seeded verified account
test_focus: Seeding twice leaves exactly one alice-dev row
The seeded account signs in with Valid-password-123! through POST /api/auth/login
The seeded account's password never appears in any API payload or log
